You are a research assistant preparing a literature review on transformer architectures in natural language processing. Your goal is to collect papers from multiple academic sources, analyze them, organize them in a knowledge base, and produce a comprehensive review document.

Start by searching the scholarly database for papers related to "transformer", then run a second, separate search for papers related to "attention mechanism" — two searches, one per phrase — and combine (union) the results, removing duplicates. Query the scholarly paper catalog through the scholarly MCP — its search-arxiv tool returns arXiv-style entries that include paper IDs, which you will need for the overlap analysis below. Retrieve all available papers and note their titles, authors, publication years, and journal references.

Next, search the arxiv repository (via the arxiv_local MCP) for papers about "transformer", then run a second, separate search for papers about "neural network" — two searches, one per phrase — and combine (union) the results, removing duplicates. Download and read through the abstracts of the papers you find to understand what each paper covers.

Write and run a Python analysis script. The script should take the collected paper data and categorize each paper into one of these methodology categories: "Architecture Design" for papers proposing new model architectures, "Training Methods" for papers about training techniques or optimization, "Applications" for papers applying transformers to specific tasks, and "Survey" for papers that review or survey the field. Assign categories based on keywords in the title and abstract. The script should also identify which papers appear in both databases (overlap analysis by matching paper IDs).

Create a database in the knowledge base titled "Research Paper Tracker" with properties for Title (title type), Paper_ID (rich_text), Authors (rich_text), Year (number), Category (select with options Architecture Design, Training Methods, Applications, Survey), Source (select with options Scholarly, Arxiv, Both), and Abstract_Summary (rich_text). Add a page entry for each unique paper found across both databases.

Create a Word document called Transformer_Literature_Review.docx in the workspace. The document should have a title "Literature Review: Transformer Architectures in NLP", followed by an introduction section explaining the scope of the review. Then include a section for each methodology category listing the papers in that category with their titles, authors, year, and a brief description from the abstract. End with a conclusion section summarizing the state of the field and identifying research gaps.

Create an Excel file called Research_Paper_Analysis.xlsx in the workspace with three sheets. The first sheet "Paper_Catalog" should have columns Paper_ID, Title, Authors, Year, Source (Scholarly, Arxiv, or Both), and Category. The second sheet "Method_Comparison" should have columns Category, Paper_Count, Avg_Year, and Key_Papers (listing titles of papers in that category). The third sheet "Citation_Matrix" should list all unique papers with columns Paper_ID, Title, In_Scholarly (Yes or No), In_Arxiv (Yes or No), and Overlap (Yes if in both, No otherwise). Write paper IDs as plain text (e.g. 1706.03762) and all other cell values as literal values — do not write Excel formulas.

Your workspace contains review_guidelines.json with category definitions and lit_review_template.md with formatting guidance.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use two dependency waves. The main agent first dynamically locates and reads review_guidelines.json and lit_review_template.md from the task-visible workspace.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly two source sub-agents in parallel:
1. explore 0 (academic-literature-researcher 0): One explore sub-agent calls the Scholarly search-arxiv tool exactly twice, once for transformer and once for attention mechanism. It returns the complete responses available from those two calls, normalized arXiv-style paper IDs, titles, authors, years, journal references, abstracts, query membership, duplicate IDs, and missing-field controls. It is strictly read-only.
2. explore 1 (academic-literature-researcher 1): One explore sub-agent owns the local-arXiv branch. It calls search_papers exactly twice for transformer and neural network with the service's largest safe result limit, deduplicates normalized IDs, then uses download_paper and read_paper for each unique result as needed to verify its abstract. It writes no final artifact; if the corpus is large, it persists one runtime-unique JSON in the discovered task workspace and returns only path/hash/counts plus compact metadata controls.

After Wave 1, the main agent reconciles IDs without losing source membership, then writes and runs the required Python analysis script. The script consumes the two verified corpora, unions by normalized Paper_ID, labels Source as Scholarly/Arxiv/Both, assigns exactly one of Architecture Design, Training Methods, Applications, Survey from the guidelines and title/abstract evidence, and emits one canonical runtime JSON containing all unique papers, overlap flags, category counts, and controls. Read the script and JSON back before Wave 2.

Wave 2 — dispatch exactly three coder sub-agents in parallel from that same canonical JSON:
1. coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): Sole owner of the exact-title Notion database Research Paper Tracker. Fully paginate search before create/reuse, block on duplicate exact-title databases/pages, enforce Title, Paper_ID, Authors, Year, Category, Source, Abstract_Summary with exact types/options, upsert one page per Paper_ID, and query/read all managed pages back.
2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 0): Sole writer of Transformer_Literature_Review.docx. Follow lit_review_template.md, use the exact title and category sections, cover every unique paper with abstract-grounded text, add evidence-based gaps, and read the document back.
3. coder 2 (office-report-builder 1): Sole writer of Research_Paper_Analysis.xlsx. Create exactly Paper_Catalog, Method_Comparison, Citation_Matrix; use plain-text IDs and literal values, preserve every source flag/category, and read all populated ranges back.

Each writer must self-correct before returning. The main agent compares only IDs, counts, categories, titles, years and overlap flags across the three receipts; no third wave or repair agent is allowed.

You are a planning sub-agent. Decompose the following task into an ordered list of subtasks, specifying for each: (a) dispatch decision — `self` (main agent), `explore` (read-only), or `coder` (execution); (b) whether it is independent/parallelizable or must wait on another subtask's output.

TASK DESCRIPTION (research assistant literature review on transformer architectures in NLP):

1. SEARCH (Scholarly): Use the scholarly MCP's search-arxiv tool to search for "transformer" (one search), then a SECOND separate search for "attention mechanism" (one search). Combine (union) results, removing duplicates. Retrieve all available papers: titles, authors, publication years, journal references, and paper IDs (arXiv-style IDs).

2. SEARCH (arXiv local): Use the arxiv_local MCP's search_papers tool to search for "transformer" (one search), then a SECOND separate search for "neural network" (one search). Combine (union) results, removing duplicates. Download and read through the abstracts of the papers found to understand coverage.

3. ANALYSIS SCRIPT: Write and run a Python analysis script that:
   - Takes the collected paper data from both databases
   - Categorizes each paper into one of: "Architecture Design" (new model architectures), "Training Methods" (training techniques/optimization), "Applications" (applying transformers to specific tasks), "Survey" (reviews/surveys the field) — based on keywords in title and abstract
   - Identifies papers appearing in BOTH databases via overlap analysis by matching paper IDs

4. KNOWLEDGE BASE (Notion): Create a database titled "Research Paper Tracker" with properties: Title (title type), Paper_ID (rich_text), Authors (rich_text), Year (number), Category (select: Architecture Design, Training Methods, Applications, Survey), Source (select: Scholarly, Arxiv, Both), Abstract_Summary (rich_text). Add a page entry for EACH unique paper found across both databases.

5. WORD DOCUMENT: Create Transformer_Literature_Review.docx with title "Literature Review: Transformer Architectures in NLP", an introduction section on review scope, one section per methodology category listing papers (titles, authors, year, brief description from abstract), and a conclusion section summarizing state of the field and research gaps.

6. EXCEL FILE: Create Research_Paper_Analysis.xlsx with three sheets:
   - "Paper_Catalog": columns Paper_ID, Title, Authors, Year, Source (Scholarly/Arxiv/Both), Category
   - "Method_Comparison": columns Category, Paper_Count, Avg_Year, Key_Papers (titles)
   - "Citation_Matrix": columns Paper_ID, Title, In_Scholarly (Yes/No), In_Arxiv (Yes/No), Overlap (Yes/No)
   - Paper IDs as plain text (e.g., 1706.03762); all values literal, NO Excel formulas.

7. WORKSPACE CONTEXT: The workspace contains review_guidelines.json (category definitions) and lit_review_template.md (formatting guidance) that must be read and followed.

Environment: The workspace root is /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace. Tools available: mcp__scholarly__* (search-arxiv, search-google-scholar), mcp__arxiv_local__* (search_papers, list_papers, read_paper, download_paper), mcp__notion__* (databases/pages), mcp__word__* (docx generation), mcp__excel__* (xlsx generation), mcp__terminal__*, mcp__local__python_execute, mcp__filesystem__*.

DELIVERABLE: Return a numbered plan with subtask order, dispatch decisions (self/explore/coder), and dependency/parallelism notes. Identify the critical path and any risks (e.g., duplicate handling across databases, large result sets, category assignment ambiguity).
Plan literature review task

You are a coder sub-agent working in the workspace:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace

CONTEXT: A literature review on Transformer architectures in NLP is being assembled. Two search datasets already exist as JSON files in the workspace:
- papers_scholarly.json (6 papers, from the scholarly search-arxiv tool: searches for "transformer" and "attention mechanism", unioned and deduped). Each entry: {id, title, authors[], year, journal, abstract}.
- papers_arxiv.json (9 papers, from the arxiv_local search_papers tool: searches for "transformer" and "neural network", unioned and deduped). Each entry: {id, title, authors[], year, abstract}.
- review_guidelines.json defines the four methodology categories and their keywords (read it).

YOUR TASKS (in order):

TASK 1 — Download and read the arxiv papers:
Using the mcp__arxiv_local__download_paper tool, download ALL 9 papers whose IDs appear in papers_arxiv.json (IDs: 2009.06732, 1706.03762, 1810.04805, 2005.14165, 1910.10683, 1409.0473, 1207.00580, 1502.03167, 1312.06199). Then use mcp__arxiv_local__read_paper on each downloaded paper to read its content (focus on the abstract). Verify that the abstracts in papers_arxiv.json match what you read; if read_paper returns a longer/more complete abstract, UPDATE papers_arxiv.json's abstract field with the fuller text (keep it concise, first 1-3 sentences is fine — the goal is understanding coverage). Record a brief one-line "coverage note" per paper (what the paper covers) — you may print these in your final report.

TASK 2 — Write and run the analysis script analyze_papers.py:
The script must:
1. Load papers_scholarly.json and papers_arxiv.json.
2. Normalize paper IDs: strip any trailing version suffix (e.g. "1706.03762v3" -> "1706.03762").
3. Union all papers across both databases into one list of UNIQUE papers (dedupe by normalized ID). For each unique paper determine Source: "Scholarly" (only in scholarly), "Arxiv" (only in arxiv), or "Both" (in both).
4. Categorize each paper into exactly one category using EXACTLY these keyword lists from review_guidelines.json (case-insensitive substring matching):
   - "Architecture Design": ["architecture", "model", "layer", "design", "structure", "mechanism"]
   - "Training Methods": ["training", "pre-training", "fine-tuning", "optimization", "learning", "scaling"]
   - "Applications": ["translation", "summarization", "classification", "generation", "task", "benchmark"]
   - "Survey": ["survey", "review", "overview", "comprehensive", "challenges", "directions"]
   Scoring rule: score(category) = (number of keyword occurrences in the TITLE) + (number of keyword occurrences in the ABSTRACT). Assign the category with the highest score. Tie-break priority order: Survey > Training Methods > Architecture Design > Applications. If all scores are 0, default to "Training Methods". (Note: match keywords as substrings; e.g. "pre-training" also matches "pretraining" only if present — do a plain substring search of each keyword in the lowercased text.)
5. Build an Abstract_Summary for each paper: a 1-2 sentence summary derived from the abstract (you may use the abstract text itself, trimmed to ~2 sentences).
6. Compute method comparison stats per category: paper count, average publication year (rounded to 1 decimal), and key papers (list of titles in that category).
7. Compute the citation matrix per unique paper: In_Scholarly (Yes/No), In_Arxiv (Yes/No), Overlap ("Yes" if in both databases else "No").
8. Write three output files into the workspace:
   - catalog.json: list of unique papers with fields: paper_id (normalized id as plain string), title, authors (comma-joined string), year (int), category, source (Scholarly/Arxiv/Both), abstract_summary, in_scholarly (bool), in_arxiv (bool).
   - method_stats.json: list of {category, paper_count, avg_year, key_papers: [titles]}.
   - citation_matrix.json: list of {paper_id, title, in_scholarly: "Yes"/"No", in_arxiv: "Yes"/"No", overlap: "Yes"/"No"}.
9. Print a clear summary: unique paper count, per-category counts, and the full categorization table (paper_id | title | category | source).

Use mcp__local__python_execute to run the script (or the terminal `python` command if you prefer). The script file analyze_papers.py should be saved in the workspace.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Only read/write files inside the workspace directory listed above.
- Do NOT modify papers_scholarly.json.
- Do not use Excel formulas, Notion, or Word tools — not needed here.
- Be precise and deterministic; the categorization must be reproducible.

DELIVERABLE (your final report): the printed categorization table summary, the per-category counts, confirmation that all 9 papers were downloaded/read and abstracts verified/updated, and the paths of the three output JSON files. Report any paper whose read content differed materially from the search-result abstract.
